text: The camp-bed in Dr. Roylott's room
why: ¶158 states the camp-bed is among the principal things in Dr. Roylott's chamber.
¶158 lists a small wooden shelf in the chamber.
¶158 says the shelf holds books, mostly of a technical character.
¶158 lists an armchair beside the bed.
¶158 lists a plain wooden chair against the wall.
¶158 lists a round table in the chamber.
¶158 lists a large iron safe in the chamber.

text: That afternoon: they go on into Dr. Roylott's chamber
why: ¶157 says they will carry their researches into the inner apartment, and ¶158 shows them entering Dr. Roylott's chamber. The afternoon setting follows from ¶116-126.

text: That afternoon: Holmes walks slowly round Dr. Roylott's chamber, examining each thing in it
why: ¶158 states Holmes walked slowly round the chamber and examined each and all of its furnishings with keen interest.

text: What made the clanging sound? — a large iron safe stands in Dr. Roylott's room
why: The safe is stated in ¶158, and Helen heard a metallic clang in ¶50 and ¶52, so the safe as a candidate source is a possibility the story gives reason to consider. The label does not state that the safe made the sound as established fact.
